purpose: Complete pre-refresh records preserved for history, not active applications or current deadlines. Current records remain in the primary data files.

grants.name: Redland City Council Community Support Grant
grants.status: Round 1 closed - Round 2 opens 12 October 2026 and closes 1 November 2026
grants.best_for: Up to $20,000 for Redland City community projects with social, cultural, recreational or environmental outcomes. Requires not-for-profit eligibility, Redland location, insurance, quotes and reporting capacity.
grants.deadline: Round 2 opens 12 October 2026 and closes 1 November 2026
grants.applicants: Incorporated not-for-profits or Act entities; unincorporated groups through an eligible auspice; registered wildlife carers are a conservation-only exception

grants.name: Screen Australia First Nations Documentary Development
grants.status: Future round — next published deadline 5:00pm AEST 22 October 2026
grants.best_for: Development of documentary projects that are genuinely First Nations-led in key creative roles, with appropriate cultural authority, ICIP practice and rights.
grants.funding: Up to $30,000 for feature or series development; up to $20,000 for a one-hour television documentary or online documentary.
grants.deadline: The 20 August 2026 deadline passed; next published deadline is 5:00pm AEST 22 October 2026, then 14 January 2027.
grants.applicants: Eligible Australian First Nations key creatives and applicant structures under Screen Australia rules; the project must be genuinely First Nations-led, not merely about First Nations people or Country.

grants.name: Redland City Council Community Celebration Grant 2026–27
grants.best_for: Community celebrations, First Nations cultural storytelling and participatory local events. Capital works and equipment purchases are excluded.
grants.deadline: Next round opens 28 September and closes 18 October 2026; further rounds are scheduled in February–March and April–May 2027.
grants.applicants: Eligible incorporated not-for-profits or auspiced groups with ABN, financial viability, $20 million public liability insurance and Redland City delivery.

grants.name: Creative Australia First Nations Arts d/Deaf and/or Disabilities Project Fund 2026
grants.best_for: Projects and professional development led by eligible First Nations d/Deaf artists or arts workers, First Nations artists or arts workers with disability, or qualifying First Nations organisations with an evidenced history of supporting those artists. Identity, disability, organisational control, cultural authority and consent must not be inferred.
grants.deadline: Closes 3:00pm AEDT Tuesday 13 October 2026; that is 2:00pm AEST in Brisbane. Account registration can take two business days.
grants.applicants: Eligible Australian First Nations d/Deaf artists or arts workers, First Nations artists or arts workers with disability, their eligible groups, or First Nations organisations with at least 51% First Nations board control and a demonstrated history of supporting eligible artists; all eligibility and assent are TO BE CONFIRMED.

grants.name: Queensland Touring Fund Round 3 2026
grants.best_for: A tour or touring program that gives regional Queensland communities access to high-quality arts and cultural work, including music gigs. It needs a developed work, viable route, presenters or venues, audience evidence and a realistic touring budget.
grants.funding: Up to $100,000 AUD for one tour or a touring program of up to 12 months, covering up to 50% of project costs; additional access funding up to $10,000 may be available
grants.deadline: Round 3 opened 31 August and closes 2:00pm AEST Monday 12 October 2026.
grants.applicants: Eligible Queensland-based artists, groups or organisations with a tour-ready arts or cultural work and an itinerary covering at least three regional Queensland locations outside the touring party's home location; applicant, co-funding, venue, contract and tour requirements remain TO BE CONFIRMED.

grants.name: Queensland Community Housing Energy Upgrades rebate
grants.level_label: Queensland Government Department of Housing and Public Works
grants.best_for: Energy-efficiency upgrades to existing Queensland community-housing dwellings that are owned and managed by an eligible registered community housing provider. It is not general housing construction, household assistance or a community-wide clean-energy grant.
grants.funding: Rebate up to $4,500 excluding GST per eligible dwelling; $18 million is the whole program pool, not an applicant cap
grants.deadline: Applications close 30 October 2026; approved installations must be completed by 30 June 2027.
grants.applicants: Active registered community housing providers listed on the national or Queensland register that own and manage eligible existing Queensland dwellings; dwelling ownership, registration, quotes, conditional approval, licensed installation and upgrade eligibility are TO BE CONFIRMED.

grants.name: National Songwriting and Recording in Schools Stimulus 2026
grants.best_for: Inclusive contemporary songwriting and recording programs for primary, secondary or tertiary learners, especially regional, remote or under-served cohorts. A school, TAFE, university, eligible music education provider, council or qualifying consortium must lead; it is not an individual artist grant or general music equipment fund.
grants.deadline: Applications close 3:00pm AEDT Tuesday 13 October 2026; application-system registration must be completed before 10:00am AEDT 12 October 2026.
grants.applicants: Eligible Australian schools, school clusters, TAFEs, universities, music academies or providers, community conservatoria, RTOs, local councils, music charities or foundations, and consortia with at least one educational institution. The lead must have an ABN, be majority Australian owned and have operated for at least two years.

grants.name: Creative Australia ACF Boost 2027
grants.best_for: A defined Australian arts or cultural project ready to run a public Australian Cultural Fund campaign from February to April 2027. It is a small matched-fundraising layer, not whole-project finance or general organisational support.
grants.funding: Dollar-for-dollar matched funding up to $5,000, plus eligible public donations raised through the Australian Cultural Fund campaign
grants.deadline: Applications close 12:00pm AEDT Monday 19 October 2026; successful campaigns run from 1 February to 30 April 2027
grants.applicants: Australian citizens or permanent residents aged 18 or over, including eligible artists, collectives and organisations with an active ABN or an auspice agreement, an eligible cultural project and capacity to run an Australian Cultural Fund campaign.

grants.name: Innovate with nbn Grants Program 2026
grants.status: Open - closes 12 October 2026; no closing time is published on business.gov.au
grants.best_for: Existing regional or remote digital businesses using the nbn network to grow technology-led ideas in agtech and environment, arts, culture and tourism, education, First Nations business, health and wellbeing, productivity or women in regional business.
grants.funding: $15,000 for one winner in each of seven categories; one category winner also receives an additional $20,000 Champion Award. $125,000 is the whole program pool.
grants.deadline: Applications close Monday 12 October 2026; no closing time is published on the official business.gov.au listing.
grants.applicants: Existing regional or remote Australian digital businesses or organisations connected to the nbn network, with an ABN and an Australian bank account matching the ABN. Category, location and operating-business eligibility remain TO BE CONFIRMED.

grants.name: Festivals Australia Round 23
grants.level_label: Australian Government Office for the Arts
grants.status: Open - closes 13 October 2026; no closing time is published on the official program page
grants.best_for: One participatory arts or cultural project delivered within an eligible regional or remote festival or significant one-off community celebration. It can support a performance, workshop, installation, exhibition or similar public arts experience, but not general festival operations, permanent LED capital or a bundle of unrelated activities.
grants.funding: No fixed applicant cap is published; the program provides approximately $1.4 million each financial year across all successful projects, which is a program envelope rather than an applicant amount
grants.deadline: Round 23 closes 13 October 2026 for projects starting from 1 February 2027. No closing time is published on the official program page.
grants.applicants: Eligible regional artists, arts workers and organisations proposing one arts or cultural project with community participation and audience engagement at a festival or significant one-off community celebration in a location confirmed as eligible by the official remoteness map.
